faqs.question: What does the Mycobacterial Identification Test measure?
faqs.answer: The Mycobacterial Identification Test identifies different species of Mycobacteria present in your sample.

faqs.question: Why is the Mycobacterial Identification Test done?
faqs.answer: • To diagnose tuberculosis and other mycobacterial infections • To determine the species of Mycobacteria causing the infection • To assess drug resistance patterns • To monitor treatment progress and effectiveness • To prevent further transmission of the disease

faqs.question: When is the Mycobacterial Identification Test recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: The Mycobacterial Identification Test is recommended when you • have symptoms suggestive of tuberculosis or mycobacterial infections, such as persistent cough, fever, weight loss, and night sweats, • are at high risk of tuberculosis due to close contact with an infected individual, or • have a positive result on preliminary tests for mycobacterial infections.

faqs.question: What if the results of the Mycobacterial Identification Test are abnormal?
faqs.answer: Abnormal results from the Mycobacterial Identification Test may indicate • active tuberculosis infection caused by specific species of Mycobacteria, • drug resistance, which may require alternative medication options, or • need for further diagnostic tests.

faqs.question: What to expect during the Mycobacterial Identification Test?
faqs.answer: During the test, a sample of pure growth of Mycobacteria will be collected from your sputum, tissue, or other relevant sources. The sample will be sent to the laboratory, where a technique called MALDI TOF (Vitek MS) will be used for analysis.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the Mycobacterial Identification Test?
faqs.answer: • Follow any additional instructions provided by your doctor or the laboratory regarding fasting or discontinuing specific medications. • Inform your doctor if you have any specific requirements.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with the Mycobacterial Identification Test?
faqs.answer: • Acid-Fast Bacillus (AFB) smear: This microscopic examination detects acid-fast bacteria in a patient's sample and is often used as an initial screening test for tuberculosis and other mycobacterial infections. • Gene Xpert MTB/RIF: This molecular test detects the presence of tuberculosis bacteria and determines resistance to rifampicin, an important anti-tuberculosis drug.

faqs.question: What is the Mycobacterial Identification Test also known as?
faqs.answer: Mycobacterial culture identification or mycobacterial species identification

faqs.question: What is tuberculosis?
faqs.answer: Tuberculosis (TB) is a contagious bacterial infection caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It primarily affects the lungs but can also affect other parts of the body. Common symptoms include cough, fever, weight loss, and fatigue.
